### Backgrounds

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Particles from the atmosphere**

Cosmic-ray showers make both muons and neutrinos.
The Earth blocks muons along long paths through rock;
atmospheric neutrinos can still pass.

$$
\Phi_\nu=\Phi_{\nu,\rm atmospheric}+\Phi_{\nu,\rm astrophysical}.
$$

An upward-going track is not automatically a cosmic-neutrino event.
Muons from the atmosphere above a detector can still reach it.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Local light in the water**

The film illustrates one decay branch in **seawater**:

$$
{}^{40}_{19}\mathrm K\longrightarrow{}^{40}_{20}\mathrm{Ca}+e^-+\bar\nu_e.
$$

The electron makes Cherenkov light; the decay antineutrino is not the optical flash.
Nearby sensors can share a flash — useful for calibration, not a cosmic-source tag.

::: {.small}
Bioluminescence is a separate background, not radioactive decay.
This seawater example is not a model of freshwater Baikal's optical background.
:::
:::
:::::

### Energy & direction

$$
P_0(E,\theta_z)=\exp\!\left[-N_A
\bigl(\sigma_{\rm CC}(E)+\sigma_{\rm NC}(E)\bigr)X(\theta_z)\right],
\qquad
X=\int_{\rm chord}\rho(r)\,d\ell.
$$

**Here $P_0$ means no interaction at all**, not the regenerated neutrino flux.
There is no universal energy above which all neutrinos stop.

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**A long path**

At $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$ through the diameter:

$$
L=12742\,\mathrm{km},\qquad P_0\simeq0.19\%.
$$
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**A shorter path**

At the same energy, $\theta_z=100^\circ$:

$$
L\simeq2213\,\mathrm{km},\qquad P_0\simeq66.2\%.
$$
:::
:::::

::: {.small}
Surface-to-surface spherical PREM model; neutrino, not antineutrino, CSMS cross sections.
$90^\circ$: horizon; $180^\circ$: upward through the centre.
:::

### Effective area

$$
N_{\rm sig}=T\int \Phi_\nu(E,\Omega)\,
A_{\rm eff}(E,\Omega)\,dE\,d\Omega.
$$

The effective area belongs to a **specified event selection**.
It accounts for propagation, interactions, detector response and selection.

::: {.takeaway}
Sensitivity depends on energy and direction — not just instrumented volume.
:::

Starting-event and surface-veto selections also open parts of the downward sky.
Their efficiencies and backgrounds must be evaluated for each analysis.

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube: a PeV-region downward-track selection](https://icecube.wisc.edu/news/research/2025/03/probing-the-high-energy-region-using-muon-neutrinos-from-the-southern-sky/).
:::

::::::

::: {.notes}
**Finish the principles block in about 2–3 minutes.** The Earth shield movie is
97.9 seconds; the independent seawater companion is 32 seconds. Formula tabs
are optional detours; do not narrate every tab in full.

The surface is NASA Blue Marble's July 2004 composite, not a live image.
First show the textured globe and atmospheric showers, then a half-globe
cutaway exposing crust, mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core.
Radii follow PREM; interior colours are schematic. Crossing particles use
one complete planar section through the detector, without folded trajectories.
Crust is not thickened; boundary lines are annotations.
Atmosphere, shower, detector and particle glyphs are enlarged for visibility.
The surface map does not define the radial density model's local geography.

The atmospheric showers reuse the Monte Carlo library from dvnanima/air_shower_cascade;
their atmosphere and lateral dimensions are enlarged for visibility. A far-side
muon cannot cross the Earth; do not claim all atmospheric muons stop before a
deep detector. Local downgoing muons are a major background. Quality cuts also
reject falsely upgoing tracks. Atmospheric and astrophysical neutrinos differ
in origin, not particle species. Direction alone does not identify their
source class. Veto selections do not reject atmospheric neutrinos universally.

Muon ranges use interpolated PDG CSDA tables: a 1 TeV muon travels about
0.93 km in standard rock (2.43 km in liquid water); the tabulated 1 PeV
rock range is about 6.4 km. Stopping distances are unresolved at planetary
scale and appear in the explicitly enlarged inset. Stochastic losses and
decay are not propagated. A second inset shows a neutrino interacting below
the detector and producing a detectable upward-going muon.

The density model is spherical PREM, including its average ocean shell;
detector depth is neglected. Chords are surface-to-surface, not exact paths
for any named telescope. Integration is split at radial discontinuities.
The diameter column is 1.0946856e10 g/cm². CSMS neutrino CC+NC cross sections
give P0=0.9474/0.6645/0.1528/0.001906 at 1/10/100/1000 TeV; at 1 PeV and
zenith 100 degrees, P0=0.661750. The packet samples first-interaction depths;
the displayed probability is calculated, not measured or inferred from the
small packet's fraction. CC/NC crosses remove symbols from the unchanged
branch. NC neutrinos are not destroyed: their lower-energy continuation and
tau regeneration require transport, which is not simulated. P0 differs from
slide 7's regenerated flux ratio. There is no sharp energy cutoff.

The companion illustrates seawater K-40's beta-minus branch, not freshwater
Baikal's background. The 0.8 MeV electron is a chosen example, not a sampled
beta spectrum; its configured threshold is about 0.264 MeV. The charged
electron supplies the optical flash, not the decay antineutrino. Electron and
antineutrino arrows are schematic: no decay-kinematics, recoil or electron
transport calculation is implied. The tiny electron path is enlarged only
in an inset, never presented as a metre-scale track in the full array.

The schematic geometry borrows ANTARES's 1 m triplet and 14.5 m storey spacing.
Whole-array symbols represent triplets; the inset resolves selected neighbours.
True group-speed flight times for chosen direct paths are shown in slow motion.
They are not sampled accepted hits. No activity, photon yield, absorption,
scattering, PMT acceptance, count/rate, coincidence efficiency or rejection
performance is calculated. Local coincidences can calibrate timing/relative
sensitivity; random coincidences are a different contribution. Bioluminescence
is not radioactive decay and is not simulated.

For the final tab, define flux before Earth attenuation and effective area
including propagation and selection; do not multiply by P0 again. Muon,
deposited and neutrino energy are distinct; the films do not reconstruct
neutrino energy or forecast telescope sensitivity.

Earth movie source, assumptions and tests: dvnanima/earth_shield/README.md
and test_earth_shield.py. Seawater companion: dvnanima/earth_filter/RADIOACTIVITY.md.
Media provenance: media/backgrounds/SOURCES.md.
[CSMS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3723);
[PREM](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7);
[ANTARES K-40 coincidences](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.4886);
[Spiering, sections 3.1.5–3.1.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::
